correctness.rationale: PASS: For arbitrary positive diagonal K and PSD L0, B=K+L0 is invertible. Sherman–Morrison gives z(t)=z0-q lambda h; h^T L0 h=r-c, with r>0,c>0, yields D(t)=D(0)+(q^2-2qa)lambda-q^2c lambda^2. Strict concavity in increasing lambda when q!=0 proves interval endpoint minimization. Sequential endpoint replacement proves the all-box-corners identity; q=0 is a true flat case. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 1105 assertions over 84 rank-one configurations and multiedge cases. No finite test was treated as proof.

value.rationale: PASS: The result solves a genuinely network-wide nonconvex design question under practically meaningful independent nonzero lower and finite upper tie-strength restrictions, reducing all continuous tie strengths to binary endpoints. The three-node example has a unique mixed optimum at weights (1/4,3), disproving any trivial all-weak/all-strong rule; the two-node example has a real strict interior maximum, demonstrating a nonmonotone tradeoff. The result does not purport to solve exponential corner selection efficiently.
